JobRunSparkUiResponse.title: JobRunSparkUiResponse
JobRunSparkUiResponse.description:
Deep link to the Databricks Spark UI for a job run.

Endpoint always returns 200; ``state`` is the discriminator. Real
HTTP errors (auth failures, server crashes) still surface as their
natural status codes and bypass this shape.

``state`` values:

- ``available``: happy path — render the link.
- ``no_spark_context``: serverless / SQL warehouse / queued run — no
  Spark UI to deep-link to. FE disables the action with a tooltip.
- ``not_found``: job or ``task_run_id`` does not exist. FE hides the
  action.
- ``workspace_mismatch``: caller-supplied ``workspace_id`` does not
  match the workspace that owns this job. FE surfaces a toast.
- ``permission_denied``: the workspace's Service Principal lacks
  View / Manage Run / Admin permission on this specific job. Won't
  resolve until an admin grants permission, so FE should surface a
  toast distinct from the transient upstream-error one.
- ``upstream_error``: Databricks credentials missing, or the upstream
  ``runs/get`` call failed for any other reason. FE surfaces a toast.

The four URL fields are present **only** when ``state == "available"``.
``message`` carries a human-readable detail for the error states.
``spark_context_id`` is fetched live from the Databricks Jobs API
(``runs/get``) because it is not ingested into ClickHouse.

WarehouseAutoTuneSavingsSummaryResponse.title: WarehouseAutoTuneSavingsSummaryResponse
WarehouseAutoTuneSavingsSummaryResponse.description:
Realised savings range + a derived annualized estimate for the two
stat blocks shown above the SQL warehouse detail tabs.

``realized_savings`` sums ``actual`` savings over the caller's
``start_date``/``end_date`` window. ``estimated_annual_savings`` is
independent of that window: it annualizes a trailing 29-day
actual+potential run-rate (capped at today), mirroring
``DatabricksSavingsService.get_overall_savings_estimate``'s
methodology, scoped to this one warehouse. Sourced entirely from
ClickHouse ``dbx_auto_tune_cost_savings`` — no Postgres insights table.

WarehouseAutoTuneSavingsTrendPoint.title: WarehouseAutoTuneSavingsTrendPoint
WarehouseAutoTuneSavingsTrendPoint.description:
One period's auto-tune savings for a SQL warehouse.

``min_cost_saved``/``max_cost_saved`` are the range underlying
``cost_saved`` for this period+savings_type — used to render a min-max
range in the Auto Tune chart tooltip (e.g. "$128.91 - $154.2"). They
default to 0.0 so existing callers that don't need the range are
unaffected.

WarehouseAutoTuneSavingsTrendsResponse.title: WarehouseAutoTuneSavingsTrendsResponse
WarehouseAutoTuneSavingsTrendsResponse.description:
Per-period auto-tune savings for a SQL warehouse, split into realized
and potential.

``actual`` holds savings while an applied auto-tune recommendation (e.g.
a lowered auto-stop) was in effect; ``potential`` holds the savings an
active, not-yet-applied recommendation would have earned over the same
window. Sourced from ClickHouse ``dbx_auto_tune_cost_savings``.

WarehouseQueryMetricsTimelinePoint.title: WarehouseQueryMetricsTimelinePoint
WarehouseQueryMetricsTimelinePoint.description:
One time bucket of the SQL warehouse Monitoring page's charts.

Sourced from the query-history timeline only — DBU/cost and
config-change (audit) events were both dropped from this endpoint
(the Monitoring page's DBUs chart and config-change markers were
removed) so every bucket here comes from exactly one source; there's
no more "billing-only bucket" concept to null-fill.

WarehouseQueryMetricsTimelineResponse.title: WarehouseQueryMetricsTimelineResponse
WarehouseQueryMetricsTimelineResponse.description:
Response for the SQL warehouse Monitoring page's metrics timeline.

``ch_data_through`` is the observed ClickHouse-mirror freshness cutover
used to route the query-history source between ClickHouse and a live
Databricks-system-tables tail (``None`` if that mirror has never
ingested a row for this tenant). ``live_tail_used`` is true if the
query-metrics source actually pulled rows from the live tail for this
response. Additive fields — the frontend schema tolerates extra
optional keys.

day_of_month.title: Day Of Month
day_of_month.description: Day of month for monthly frequency (1-31). Only valid when frequency='monthly'. When omitted, defaults to the 1st. Follows standard cron semantics: schedules with day_of_month=29/30/31 only fire in months that contain that day (so day=31 skips February, April, June, September, November).
